docs.title: iVedha Managed Elasticsearch Platform
docs.text:
Deploy and operate Elasticsearch and Kibana in your Azure subscription through an Azure Marketplace Managed Application. iVedha manages the supported platform lifecycle, with Opsflw providing deployment and operations automation.

The platform provides a managed foundation for search, observability, analytics, and eligible AI use cases without requiring the customer to build and operate the underlying Azure and Elastic platform alone.

The platform runs in the customer's Azure subscription. The customer owns the subscription, connectivity, identity, DNS, and data onboarding. iVedha/Opsflw manages platform deployment and operations through supported managed application interfaces and automation.

docs.title: What the platform provides
docs.text:
The Azure Managed Application creates a customer-visible application resource and a managed resource group containing the platform infrastructure. Elasticsearch and Kibana run on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), with supporting Azure services for networking, secrets and certificates, storage, monitoring, and lifecycle operations.

The exact resources, capacity, topology, endpoints, and licensed features depend on the selected Marketplace plan and deployed platform version.

Capability Typical use Elasticsearch Index, search, and analyze application, operational, business, or vector data Kibana Explore data, build dashboards, and perform supported administration Managed Azure runtime Run the platform on AKS in the customer's Azure subscription Public or private access Connect users and data sources using the approved network model Managed lifecycle Provision, reconcile, monitor, maintain, and upgrade the supported platform

This is not Elastic Cloud hosted outside the customer environment, and it is not an unmanaged Kubernetes package. Customers use the managed application, Elasticsearch, Kibana, and documented customer actions rather than modifying managed infrastructure directly.

For the detailed component and Azure resource model, see architecture details and platform components.

docs.title: Who manages what
docs.text:
Customer iVedha / Opsflw Azure subscription, billing, policy, and quota Managed application provisioning and reconciliation Network routes, Private Endpoints, and DNS Platform configuration and supported lifecycle actions Microsoft Entra identity and customer access decisions Platform health monitoring and managed operations Data onboarding, data governance, and workload outcomes Supported maintenance, upgrades, and troubleshooting Elastic license and customer-managed integrations Customer-facing deployment details and managed support workflows

The managed application does not transfer ownership of the customer's Azure subscription, identities, network, DNS, or data to iVedha. Some managed-resource platform telemetry is sent to iVedha operations for platform health monitoring; customer Elasticsearch indices and application data remain customer-owned.

For detailed task-level ownership and safety boundaries, see shared responsibility.

docs.title: Choose public or private connectivity
docs.text:
Choose the access model before deployment.

  • Public connectivity uses internet-reachable service endpoints with TLS, authentication, and deployment-supported access restrictions.
  • Private connectivity uses Azure Private Endpoint connectivity and requires customer-managed routing, private DNS, and certificate trust where applicable.

For the decision criteria and required ownership, see plan connectivity.

docs.title: What AI-ready means
docs.text:
AI-ready means the platform can provide the Elasticsearch and Kibana foundation for eligible full-text search, vector search, inference, machine-learning, and AI-assisted use cases. It does not mean every AI feature or external model service is enabled by default.

Before using an AI capability, verify the deployed Elastic version and license, selected topology and capacity, required integrations and outbound connectivity, and your organization's security and data-governance requirements.

docs.title: Follow the customer journey
docs.text:
1. Plan — decide the Azure subscription, region, capacity, topology, connectivity, DNS, TLS approach, maintenance window, and owners.
  2. Deploy — create the managed application from the approved Azure Marketplace offer and monitor platform readiness.
  3. Next Steps — reset the administrator password, complete network, DNS, and TLS configuration, and verify Elasticsearch and Kibana access.
  4. Operate — configure access, onboard data, use the platform, monitor health and capacity, and perform supported lifecycle tasks.
  5. Get Help — identify the failing layer, collect safe evidence, and use the managed support path when needed.
  6. Reference — look up architecture, responsibilities, deployment fields, lifecycle states, permissions, capacity, compatibility, limits, and terms.

Before you deploy

Be ready to choose your Azure region, workload profile, capacity, topology, connectivity model, DNS ownership, certificate approach, maintenance window, and support contacts.

Start with the planning overview. For another iVedha application, return to the Opsflw documentation catalog.

docs.title: Limits and checklists
docs.text:
Use this page as a quick operational reference.

Platform limits depend on the Marketplace plan, Azure subscription, deployed platform version, Elastic license, and workload configuration.

Do not assume limits from another deployment apply to yours.

docs.title: Capacity and service limits
docs.text:
For planning, use the supported Small, Medium, and Large capacity profiles.

Actual supported workload depends on factors such as:

  • ingestion rate;
  • stored data;
  • retention;
  • replicas;
  • query activity;
  • OpenTelemetry volume;
  • integrations;
  • workload growth.

If usage approaches the current deployment capacity, request a capacity review through iVedha rather than changing managed infrastructure directly.

See Monitor health and capacity.

docs.title: Before deployment
docs.text:
Use the dedicated Deployment checklist.

Confirm:

  • Azure and Marketplace prerequisites;
  • target subscription and region;
  • workload and initial capacity;
  • public-access choice;
  • DNS-domain choice;
  • maintenance window;
  • monitored support email.

docs.text:

  • [ ] Administrator access has been established.

docs.title: Before onboarding data
docs.text:
Confirm:

  • [ ] The intended onboarding path is understood.
  • [ ] Required users or API keys use least privilege.
  • [ ] Fleet policies and integrations are defined where required.
  • [ ] OpenTelemetry instrumentation or Collector configuration is ready where required.
  • [ ] Expected data streams, datasets, or indices are known.
  • [ ] Retention requirements are understood.

For observability workloads, prefer the supported OpenTelemetry-first architecture.

docs.title: Before a platform change
docs.text:
Before requesting a capacity, maintenance, SSO, TLS, license, or other managed-platform change:

  • [ ] Identify the deployment.
  • [ ] Understand the business impact.
  • [ ] Confirm the requested configuration.
  • [ ] Identify affected applications and users.
  • [ ] Define how the change will be validated.
  • [ ] Confirm any required rollback or recovery considerations.

Use the supported iVedha workflow for platform-level changes.

docs.title: Before an upgrade
docs.text:
Confirm:

  • [ ] Current platform and Elastic versions are known.
  • [ ] Application and client compatibility has been reviewed.
  • [ ] Elastic Agent and Fleet compatibility has been reviewed.
  • [ ] OpenTelemetry Collector, SDK, and integration compatibility has been reviewed where applicable.
  • [ ] Logstash or connector compatibility has been reviewed where applicable.
  • [ ] Important workloads have a post-upgrade validation plan.

See Prepare for upgrades.

docs.title: Before certificate renewal
docs.text:
Confirm:

  • [ ] Current certificate expiration is known.
  • [ ] Required service hostnames are still correct.
  • [ ] The new platform-generated CSR has been obtained.
  • [ ] The CSR covers Kibana, Elasticsearch, Fleet, and Logstash where applicable.
  • [ ] The approved CA will sign the CSR.
  • [ ] The private key remains inside the managed platform.

See Renew TLS certificates.

docs.title: Before deletion
docs.text:
Confirm:

  • [ ] The deployment is no longer required.
  • [ ] Ingestion and applications have been stopped or redirected.
  • [ ] Data that must be retained has been identified.
  • [ ] Required backup or recovery arrangements have been confirmed.
  • [ ] Customer-owned Private Endpoints and DNS records have been identified.
  • [ ] Credentials and integrations that require cleanup have been identified.
  • [ ] Marketplace or billing implications have been reviewed.

See Delete the application.

docs.title: Need assistance
docs.text:
Use:

  • AI chat: https://chat.ivedha.cloud
  • Support portal: https://support.ivedha.com/

Do not include passwords, API keys, tokens, private keys, or other secrets in support evidence.

docs.title: Architecture details
docs.text:
The managed platform combines the Elastic Stack with Azure infrastructure and iVedha-managed operations.

The platform runs in the customer's Azure subscription while iVedha provides supported monitoring, configuration, lifecycle management, and operational assistance.

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text: The diagram is conceptual. The exact Azure resources depend on the Marketplace plan, deployment configuration, region, and platform version.

docs.title: Elasticsearch
docs.text:
Elasticsearch provides the core data platform for:

  • search;
  • indexing;
  • analytics;
  • observability data;
  • vector and semantic search.

Customer data remains in the Elasticsearch deployment running in the customer's Azure subscription.

docs.title: Kibana
docs.text:
Kibana provides the primary user interface for:

  • search and analytics;
  • dashboards and visualization;
  • observability;
  • Fleet;
  • users and roles;
  • supported Elasticsearch administration.

docs.title: Elastic Agent
docs.text:
Elastic Agent is the standard collection layer for observability workloads.

It can:

  • collect host and infrastructure telemetry;
  • collect Kubernetes telemetry;
  • receive application OpenTelemetry data;
  • run supported Elastic integrations;
  • forward logs, metrics, and traces into Elasticsearch.

docs.title: Fleet
docs.text:
Fleet centrally manages Elastic Agents.

Fleet controls:

  • agent enrollment;
  • agent policies;
  • integrations;
  • configuration distribution;
  • health;
  • agent lifecycle.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
The managed observability architecture is OpenTelemetry-first.

OpenTelemetry provides the common telemetry model for:

  • logs;
  • metrics;
  • traces.

Elastic Agent and supported integrations collect or receive telemetry and align new observability workloads with OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and OTel-native data streams.

Existing ECS-compatible integrations can continue to operate where required.

docs.title: Logstash
docs.text:
Logstash can be used when existing or specialized ingestion pipelines require transformation, routing, or protocol handling not covered by the standard Elastic Agent integration model.

For new observability onboarding, prefer Elastic Agent and OpenTelemetry unless there is a specific requirement for Logstash.

docs.title: Azure infrastructure
docs.text:
The platform uses Azure services to provide the required compute, networking, security, and storage.

Typical components include:

  • Azure Kubernetes Service;
  • Azure Key Vault;
  • Azure Storage;
  • Azure networking;
  • managed identities;
  • Azure RBAC;
  • Private Link where private connectivity is used.

The exact resource layout can change between platform versions.

Customers should not depend on internal resource names or modify managed infrastructure directly.

docs.title: Customer and managed boundaries
docs.text:
Boundary Responsibility Azure subscription Customer Managed platform infrastructure iVedha-managed Customer networking and DNS Customer Elasticsearch application data Customer Elasticsearch platform operations iVedha Application users and data access Customer Platform health monitoring iVedha Application and workload monitoring Customer Elastic Agent policies and integrations Customer, with iVedha assistance Managed lifecycle actions iVedha-supported workflow

For detailed ownership, see Shared responsibility.

docs.title: Operational control
docs.text:
Supported platform-level configuration and lifecycle actions are performed through the iVedha AI chat application:

https://chat.ivedha.cloud

Examples include:

  • administrator password reset;
  • maintenance-window changes;
  • SSO configuration;
  • TLS certificate configuration;
  • license changes;
  • supported capacity changes.

The support portal is available for tracked cases and engineering investigation:

https://support.ivedha.com/

Do not modify Kubernetes resources, secrets, Elasticsearch infrastructure, or other managed platform components directly unless the documentation explicitly identifies the action as customer-managed.

docs.title: Platform monitoring
docs.text:
The managed platform forwards operational health telemetry to the iVedha operations environment.

This telemetry is used to monitor supported platform components and investigate platform conditions.

Managed monitoring does not mean that customer Elasticsearch data is moved into the iVedha operations environment.

Customer application data remains in the customer's managed Elasticsearch deployment.

docs.title: Observability data flow
docs.text:
The preferred observability architecture is:

Applications / Hosts / Kubernetes / Azure Services
                         ↓
                    Elastic Agent
                         ↓
               Fleet-managed policy
                         ↓
             OpenTelemetry telemetry
                         ↓
                    Elasticsearch
                         ↓
                       Kibana

OpenTelemetry provides the common logs, metrics, and traces model while Fleet and Elastic Agent provide centralized collection and management.

docs.title: Search data flow
docs.text:
Application search data typically follows a simpler path:

Application / Data Pipeline
          ↓
     Elasticsearch API
          ↓
      Elasticsearch
          ↓
   Application / Kibana

Search documents do not need to use the OpenTelemetry telemetry model.

docs.title: Public access
docs.text:
When public access is enabled, supported platform services can be reached through public HTTPS endpoints.

TLS and authentication are still required.

Company security controls can further restrict which clients are permitted to use the endpoints.

docs.title: Private access
docs.text:
When public access is disabled, customers establish private connectivity using Azure Private Link.

The customer creates a Private Endpoint using the Private Link Service information provided for the deployment.

Private access requires:

  • an approved Private Endpoint;
  • network routing;
  • private DNS;
  • trusted TLS certificates.

docs.title: DNS and service hostnames
docs.text:
The deployment provides the authoritative service hostnames.

Depending on enabled components, these can include:

  • Elasticsearch;
  • Kibana;
  • Fleet;
  • Logstash.

Do not construct hostnames from internal Azure resource names.

The platform-generated CSR contains the SANs required for the deployment services.

docs.title: Data remains in the customer environment
docs.text:
The core design principle is that Elasticsearch data remains in the customer's Azure subscription.

iVedha operates and monitors the platform without requiring customer application data to be hosted in a separate iVedha Elasticsearch environment.

This provides a managed operating model while preserving customer control of the Azure subscription and data location.

docs.title: Available stack versions
docs.text: New iVedha Managed Elasticsearch Platform deployments use Elastic Stack 9.5.0. The Azure Marketplace deployment experience does not provide a stack version selector. The approved version is part of the managed platform release, not a capacity, topology, or Marketplace plan choice.

docs.title: Available version for new deployments
docs.text:
Deployment type Elastic Stack version Availability New managed deployment 9.5.0 Current approved version Existing managed deployment Deployment-specific Check the deployed version before planning a change

The stack version applies to Elasticsearch, Kibana, Fleet Server, Elastic Agent, the Elastic Distribution of OpenTelemetry Collector, Logstash, and Elastic connectors when those components are included in the deployment. A component can have its own release cycle, but iVedha validates the managed combination rather than offering independent component version selection.

Note

The version policy for Elastic Cloud Hosted does not apply to this Azure managed application. In particular, do not assume that every non-EOL release or the latest two minor releases can be selected for a new deployment.

docs.title: How versions become available
docs.text:
A new Elastic release is not automatically available in the managed platform. Before changing the new-deployment target, iVedha validates the coordinated component versions, upgrade sequence, recovery evidence, known issues, and representative platform functions. The approved version is then applied to new deployments and recorded on this page.

Release candidates and other pre-GA builds are not available as Marketplace deployment choices. Use a separately approved non-production process if iVedha support asks you to validate a preview build.

docs.title: Check an existing deployment
docs.text:
Do not infer an existing deployment's version from this page. Record the exact versions from the managed application deployment details and from the product:

  • use GET / or an approved Kibana view for Elasticsearch;
  • use the Kibana help or status view for Kibana;
  • check Fleet for Elastic Agent and integration versions;
  • record the managed platform version from deployment details or outputs.

Use compatibility to validate clients, integrations, features, and licenses against that deployment baseline.

docs.title: Plan a version change
docs.text:
Existing deployments do not change merely because the version for new deployments changes. Use only the managed upgrade or maintenance process approved for your deployment. Do not upgrade Elasticsearch, Kibana, Elastic Agent, or managed Kubernetes resources directly.

Before an upgrade:

  1. Record the current versions and target version.
  2. Review Elastic breaking changes, known issues, and client compatibility for the complete path.
  3. Verify a recent successful snapshot and recovery plan.
  4. Test representative ingestion, search, dashboards, authentication, and integrations in non-production.
  5. Agree on the maintenance window, validation owner, and recovery decision.

Follow prepare for upgrades for the complete checklist. Elasticsearch does not support downgrades; recovery is a managed service decision rather than a package rollback.

docs.title: Maintenance and end of life
docs.text: Availability in this managed platform does not extend Elastic's maintenance or support period. Review the Elastic version maintenance and support policy when planning a deployment or upgrade. If the deployed version is approaching the end of its maintenance or support period, contact iVedha support to plan a supported target and maintenance path.

docs.title: Renew TLS certificates
docs.text:
Renew customer-provided TLS certificates before they expire.

Certificate renewal uses the same supported workflow as initial certificate configuration:

https://chat.ivedha.cloud

The platform generates the private key and certificate signing request (CSR). The private key remains inside the managed platform.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Review:

  • the current certificate expiration date;
  • the service hostnames covered by the certificate;
  • the certificate authority that will issue the replacement;
  • any internal approval or renewal process required by your organization.

Start renewal early enough to allow time for certificate approval, issuance, upload, and validation.

docs.title: Request a new CSR
docs.text:
1. Sign in to the iVedha AI chat application.
  2. Select or identify the deployment.
  3. Ask the assistant to renew the TLS certificate.
  4. Complete identity verification when requested.
  5. Request a new CSR.
  6. Save the CSR provided by the platform.

The platform generates a single CSR that covers all required service hostnames for the deployment, including:

  • Kibana;
  • Elasticsearch;
  • Fleet;
  • Logstash.

The required hostnames are included as Subject Alternative Names (SANs) in the CSR.

Do not generate your own CSR or private key. The private key associated with the CSR remains inside the managed platform.

docs.title: Sign the CSR
docs.text:
Submit the CSR to your approved certificate authority.

The issued certificate must:

  • match the CSR;
  • include the required service hostnames;
  • include the required intermediate certificate chain;
  • be trusted by the clients that access the platform.

docs.title: Upload the renewed certificate
docs.text:
After the certificate is issued:

  1. Return to the iVedha AI chat.
  2. Select the same deployment.
  3. Continue the certificate-renewal workflow.
  4. Upload the issued certificate and required intermediate certificates.
  5. Confirm the change.
  6. Wait for confirmation that the certificate has been applied.

Allow a few minutes for the renewed certificate to synchronize across the platform.

docs.title: Verify the renewed certificate
docs.text:
Verify each service hostname that uses the renewed certificate.

SERVICE_HOSTNAME="<service-hostname>"

openssl s_client \
  -connect "${SERVICE_HOSTNAME}:443" \
  -servername "${SERVICE_HOSTNAME}" \
  -verify_return_error </dev/null

Confirm:

  • Verify return code: 0 (ok);
  • the expected hostname is covered;
  • the issuer is correct;
  • the new expiration date is present;
  • the expected certificate chain is served.

Then verify:

  • Kibana sign-in;
  • Elasticsearch access;
  • Fleet connectivity when applicable;
  • Logstash connectivity when applicable;
  • Elastic Agents return to or remain Healthy.

docs.title: If the old certificate is still served
docs.text:
Allow a few minutes for synchronization and test again.

If the old certificate remains after the expected propagation period, use:

  • AI chat: https://chat.ivedha.cloud
  • Support portal: https://support.ivedha.com/

Provide the deployment reference and the affected hostname.

Do not include private keys or other secrets.

docs.title: Plan the next renewal
docs.text:
Record the new expiration date in your organization's certificate-management process.

Schedule the next renewal early enough to avoid an emergency certificate replacement.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
Compatibility depends on the exact platform release, Elastic version, enabled components, integrations, and client software used by the deployment.

Do not choose client or integration versions based only on the documentation publication date.

docs.title: What to check
docs.text: Component Check Managed platform Confirm the platform release associated with the deployment Elasticsearch Confirm the exact Elasticsearch version Kibana Confirm compatibility with the deployed Elasticsearch version Fleet Server Confirm compatibility with the deployed Elastic Stack Elastic Agent Confirm the Agent version is supported by the deployed Fleet and Elasticsearch versions Fleet integrations Confirm the integration package is supported by the deployed Elastic version OpenTelemetry Collector Confirm Collector, receiver, processor, exporter, and OTLP compatibility OpenTelemetry SDKs Confirm application SDK and instrumentation compatibility Logstash Confirm Logstash and plugin compatibility with the deployed Elasticsearch version Elastic connectors Confirm connector availability, version, and license requirements Elastic license Confirm required features are included in the active license Azure region and plan Confirm the Marketplace plan and required Azure services are supported in the selected region

docs.title: Elasticsearch
docs.text:
You can identify the Elasticsearch version using an authenticated request to GET / or from an appropriate Kibana view.

When using language clients, Beats or legacy collectors, Logstash, integrations, or plugins, follow Elastic's compatibility guidance for the deployed version.

Avoid upgrading clients or ingestion components independently without first confirming compatibility.

docs.title: Elastic Agent and Fleet
docs.text:
Fleet Server, Elastic Agent, and integration packages have their own compatibility requirements.

Before deploying or upgrading an Agent:

  1. confirm the deployed Elastic Stack version;
  2. confirm the supported Elastic Agent version;
  3. confirm required integration packages are available;
  4. test representative telemetry after the change.

Do not assume the newest Elastic Agent is automatically appropriate for an older deployment.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Collector
docs.text:
OpenTelemetry Collector compatibility includes more than the Collector version itself.

Check:

  • Collector distribution;
  • receivers;
  • processors;
  • exporters;
  • extensions;
  • OTLP protocol support;
  • authentication;
  • TLS;
  • semantic-convention behavior.

If the Collector sends telemetry to Elastic, confirm the configuration is supported by the deployed Elastic version.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry SDKs and instrumentation
docs.text:
Application instrumentation can evolve independently of the backend.

Before upgrading an OpenTelemetry SDK or instrumentation library, consider:

  • semantic-convention changes;
  • resource attributes;
  • metric-name changes;
  • histogram behavior;
  • trace propagation;
  • log signal support.

Changes in instrumentation can change the fields and datasets visible in Elasticsearch even when the platform itself has not changed.

docs.title: Fleet integrations
docs.text:
Fleet integration packages can have minimum Elastic or Kibana version requirements.

An integration visible in upstream Elastic documentation might not be available in every deployed platform version.

Use the integrations available in the deployed Fleet environment as the authoritative starting point.

For new observability onboarding, prefer supported OpenTelemetry-native integrations where available.

docs.title: Logstash
docs.text:
When Logstash is used, check compatibility for:

  • Logstash version;
  • Elasticsearch output;
  • input and filter plugins;
  • pipeline syntax;
  • authentication and TLS behavior.

Do not upgrade individual Logstash plugins without understanding their compatibility with the managed platform.

docs.title: Elastic connectors
docs.text:
Connector availability can depend on:

  • Elasticsearch version;
  • Kibana version;
  • connector version;
  • Elastic license;
  • external service compatibility.

Confirm these requirements before building a production workflow around a connector.

docs.title: Elastic license
docs.text:
Some Elastic capabilities depend on the active license.

Before enabling a feature, confirm that the deployed license includes it.

iVedha can assist with:

  • license requirements;
  • license installation;
  • procurement;
  • renewal;
  • available licensing options.

See manage the Elastic license.

docs.title: Before making a compatibility-sensitive change
docs.text:
Confirm:

  1. the current platform and Elastic versions;
  2. the component or integration being changed;
  3. the supported version relationship;
  4. any license requirements;
  5. whether configuration or data-format behavior changes;
  6. how you will validate the workload after the change.

For managed platform upgrades, use the supported iVedha upgrade workflow rather than upgrading platform components independently.

See prepare for upgrades.

docs.title: Version matrices
docs.text:
This documentation intentionally does not publish a single global compatibility matrix.

Supported combinations can change between platform releases and integration-package versions.

The deployed platform version, available Fleet integrations, Elastic documentation, and supported iVedha workflows should be used together to determine compatibility for a specific deployment.

See available stack versions for the verified target used by new managed deployments. That target does not replace the exact version baseline of an existing deployment.

docs.title: Choose a data onboarding path
docs.text:
The managed platform uses OpenTelemetry as the standard observability data model.

For observability workloads:

  • OpenTelemetry provides the common telemetry model for logs, metrics, and traces;
  • Elastic Agent provides the standard collection and telemetry gateway layer;
  • Fleet provides centralized management of Elastic Agents, policies, and integrations;
  • Elasticsearch stores and analyzes the resulting telemetry;
  • Kibana provides visualization, investigation, and observability workflows.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry-first observability
docs.text:
For new observability workloads, prefer OpenTelemetry conventions and OpenTelemetry-native telemetry wherever supported.

The goal is to provide a consistent representation of telemetry from:

  • applications;
  • servers and virtual machines;
  • Kubernetes;
  • Azure services;
  • databases and middleware;
  • network and security systems;
  • custom sources.

Elastic integrations that produce ECS-compatible events remain supported, but new observability designs should move toward OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and OTel-native data streams where available.

docs.title: Choose by workload
docs.text: Data source Recommended onboarding path Application logs, metrics, and traces Elastic Agent with OpenTelemetry integrations Servers and virtual machines Elastic Agent with OpenTelemetry integrations Kubernetes Elastic Agent with OpenTelemetry integrations Azure services Elastic Agent with OpenTelemetry integrations Network and appliance telemetry Elastic Agent integrations, normalized for the observability pipeline Existing Logstash pipelines Logstash where required for existing pipelines Application search documents Elasticsearch API Existing Elasticsearch deployment Migration or reindex process

docs.title: Observability data
docs.text:
For logs, metrics, and traces, use Elastic Agent with OpenTelemetry integrations as the preferred architecture.

Elastic Agent can collect or receive telemetry from applications, infrastructure, Kubernetes, Azure services, and supported integrations. Fleet centrally manages the agents and their policies.

The resulting observability data should follow OpenTelemetry conventions where supported.

See Manage Elastic Agents with Fleet, then continue with onboard observability data.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry data streams
docs.text:
OpenTelemetry-native telemetry is stored using signal-specific data streams. Typical patterns include:

Signal Data stream pattern Logs logs-*.otel-* Metrics metrics-*.otel-* Traces traces-*.otel-*

ECS-compatible streams can continue to exist for integrations and existing workloads that require them.

docs.title: Search and application data
docs.text:
Application search data is different from observability telemetry.

Search documents, knowledge content, vector data, and application records are typically sent directly to Elasticsearch using the Elasticsearch API. These documents do not need to be represented as OpenTelemetry telemetry.

Continue with onboard search data.

docs.title: Existing pipelines
docs.text:
Existing Logstash and ECS-based pipelines can continue to operate when required.

For new observability onboarding, prefer the OpenTelemetry-first architecture unless there is a specific compatibility requirement.

docs.title: Use the deployment endpoints
docs.text:
Use only the Elasticsearch, Fleet, and other endpoints provided for your deployment.

The source system must be able to:

  • resolve the endpoint hostname;
  • reach the endpoint over the configured network path;
  • trust the TLS certificate;
  • authenticate using an approved credential.

Do not use administrator credentials for normal data ingestion.

docs.title: Start small
docs.text:
Before onboarding the full production workload:

  1. configure one representative source;
  2. verify that Elastic Agent is receiving or collecting the telemetry;
  3. confirm logs, metrics, or traces are represented correctly;
  4. verify the expected OpenTelemetry attributes and resource metadata;
  5. confirm the data appears in the expected Elasticsearch data streams;
  6. validate the data in Kibana;
  7. then expand onboarding to additional sources.

docs.title: Need help choosing?
docs.text:
Use:

  • AI chat: https://chat.ivedha.cloud
  • Support portal: https://support.ivedha.com/

For the next step, choose either:

  • Manage Elastic Agents with Fleet
  • Onboard observability data
  • Onboard search data

docs.title: Delete the application
docs.text:
Deleting the Azure Managed Application removes the managed application and its managed resource group.

Treat deletion as a permanent decommissioning action.

docs.title: Before deletion
docs.text:
Before deleting the deployment:

  • confirm that the application is no longer required;
  • stop or redirect applications and ingestion sources;
  • identify any Elasticsearch data that must be retained;
  • confirm recovery or retention requirements with iVedha when required;
  • identify customer-owned DNS records and Private Endpoints that will need to be removed;
  • identify application credentials, API keys, and integrations that should be revoked.

For observability deployments, also plan to:

  • unenroll or reassign Elastic Agents;
  • update Fleet policies where required;
  • redirect OpenTelemetry exporters or integrations to another destination.

docs.title: Preserve required data
docs.text:
If data must be retained after the deployment is deleted, coordinate the retention or recovery requirement with iVedha before deletion.

Elasticsearch snapshots can protect Elasticsearch data, but snapshot retention and access after platform deletion depend on the deployed backup configuration.

Do not delete the platform until required recovery data has been confirmed.

For assistance, see back up and restore.

docs.title: Delete the Azure Managed Application
docs.text:
In the Azure portal:

  1. Open the deployed Azure Managed Application.
  2. Confirm that you selected the correct deployment.
  3. Select Delete.
  4. Confirm the deletion when prompted.
  5. Monitor the Azure operation until the Managed Application is removed.

Do not manually delete individual resources inside the managed resource group to speed up deletion.

Deleting individual managed resources can leave the deployment in an inconsistent state.

docs.title: What deletion removes
docs.text:
Deletion of the Managed Application removes the managed Azure resources associated with the deployment.

This includes the managed platform infrastructure deployed inside the managed resource group.

Customer-owned resources outside the managed resource group might not be removed automatically.

docs.title: Remove customer-owned connectivity
docs.text:
After the managed application has been deleted, remove customer-owned resources that are no longer required.

This can include:

  • Azure Private Endpoints;
  • private DNS records;
  • public DNS records for company-owned domains;
  • firewall or allowlist rules;
  • routing configuration created specifically for the deployment.

Do not remove shared networking or DNS resources used by other applications.

docs.title: Remove credentials and integrations
docs.text:
Revoke or remove credentials that were created specifically for the deployment.

Examples include:

  • application API keys;
  • local Elastic users that are no longer required;
  • SSO application credentials;
  • integration credentials;
  • automation secrets.

For observability workloads, also remove or update:

  • Elastic Agent policies;
  • enrollment configuration;
  • OpenTelemetry exporters;
  • application telemetry destinations.

docs.title: Check Marketplace and billing state
docs.text:
After deletion, confirm that the Marketplace subscription or commercial arrangement associated with the deployment is in the expected state.

Deleting Azure resources and changing Marketplace commercial terms are separate concerns.

If you are unsure whether any Marketplace action is still required, contact iVedha.

docs.title: Need help before deletion
docs.text:
For assistance with decommissioning, data retention, or Marketplace status:

  • AI chat: https://chat.ivedha.cloud
  • Support portal: https://support.ivedha.com/

Provide the deployment reference and describe the intended decommissioning date.

Do not include passwords, API keys, private keys, or other secrets.

Warning

Do not delete the Managed Application until any required data-retention or recovery plan has been confirmed.

docs.title: Deploy from Azure Marketplace
docs.text:
Use Azure Marketplace to create the managed application in your Azure subscription.

Have the values selected during planning available before starting the deployment.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Confirm that:

  • the Azure and Marketplace prerequisites are complete;
  • the deployment checklist is complete;
  • you have permission to purchase and deploy the managed application.

docs.title: Open the Marketplace offer
docs.text:
1. In the Azure portal, open the Marketplace listing for iVedha Managed Elasticsearch Platform published by iVedha.
  2. Select the plan you want to deploy.
  3. Review the plan pricing and terms.
  4. Select Create.

docs.title: Configure the Azure deployment
docs.text:
On Basics, select:

  • Azure subscription;
  • resource group;
  • Azure region;
  • managed application name.

Use values that follow your organization's Azure naming and deployment requirements.

docs.title: Choose the platform configuration
docs.text:
Select the values chosen during planning:

  • Workload — Search or Observability;
  • Capacity — Small, Medium, or Large;
  • Topology — one of the options available for the selected workload and plan;
  • Machine learning — enable only if required and available.

See choose capacity and topology if you need to review these options.

docs.title: Configure public access
docs.text:
Choose whether to enable access over the internet.

  • Enabled — the platform exposes supported public HTTPS endpoints.
  • Disabled — private connectivity is configured after deployment.

If public access is disabled, the deployment still completes before you create the customer-side Private Endpoint and DNS configuration.

docs.title: Choose the DNS domain
docs.text:
Choose the DNS domain option selected during planning:

  • Platform-provided DNS domain — use the domain and hostnames provided by the platform.
  • Company-owned DNS domain — use a domain or subdomain owned by your organization.

If you select a company-owned DNS domain, enter the required domain value in the Marketplace form.

Do not create DNS records yet. The platform publishes the authoritative endpoint and DNS information after deployment.

docs.title: Configure maintenance
docs.text:
Select the planned maintenance settings exposed by the Marketplace form, such as:

  • occurrence or frequency;
  • day;
  • start time;
  • time zone;
  • duration.

These settings define the preferred window for supported platform maintenance.

docs.title: Provide support contacts
docs.text:
Enter the required operational or support contacts.

Use organization-approved contact information.

Do not enter passwords, tokens, private keys, or other secrets in contact or free-text fields.

docs.title: Complete plan-specific settings
docs.text:
Complete any additional settings required by the selected Marketplace plan.

This can include licensing or other plan-specific options.

For a detailed explanation of the form fields, see deployment options.

docs.title: Review and create
docs.text:
On Review + create:

  1. Resolve any Azure validation errors.
  2. Review the subscription, region, and managed application name.
  3. Verify the workload, capacity, and topology.
  4. Verify the public-access setting.
  5. Verify the DNS domain option and domain value, if applicable.
  6. Verify the maintenance window and contacts.
  7. Review the price and Marketplace terms.
  8. Select Create.

docs.title: Continue to deployment status
docs.text:
Azure first creates the Managed Application and its deployment resources.

A successful Azure deployment does not necessarily mean Elasticsearch and Kibana are ready for use. Platform provisioning and configuration continue after the Azure resources are created.

Do not modify resources in the managed resource group.

Continue to monitor deployment.

docs.title: Deployment checklist
docs.text:
Use this checklist before opening the Azure Marketplace deployment form.

You do not need to complete detailed DNS, certificate, or private networking configuration before deployment. Those steps are completed after the platform publishes its deployment details.

docs.title: Azure and Marketplace
docs.text:
• [ ] The target Azure subscription is confirmed.
  • [ ] The Azure region is confirmed.
  • [ ] Marketplace purchasing is enabled.
  • [ ] The deploying user has the required Azure permissions.
  • [ ] Azure quota and policy allow the deployment.
  • [ ] The required Marketplace offer and plan are available.

See Azure and Marketplace prerequisites.

docs.title: Platform configuration
docs.text:
• [ ] The current stack version is compatible with planned clients and integrations.
  • [ ] Search or Observability is selected.
  • [ ] The initial Small, Medium, or Large capacity is selected.
  • [ ] A supported topology is selected.
  • [ ] Optional machine-learning capacity is selected only if required.

See choose capacity and topology.

docs.title: Access and DNS domain
docs.text:
• [ ] Public access is enabled or disabled.
  • [ ] The platform-provided DNS domain or a company-owned DNS domain is selected.
  • [ ] If a company-owned DNS domain is selected, the DNS owner can create records after deployment.

Detailed endpoint, DNS, Private Endpoint, and TLS configuration is completed after deployment.

See plan connectivity.

docs.title: Maintenance and support
docs.text:
• [ ] The maintenance window and time zone are selected.
  • [ ] The service or application owner is known.
  • [ ] The technical contact is known.
  • [ ] The support or escalation contact is known.

docs.title: Ready to deploy
docs.text:
If all required items are complete, continue to Deploy from Azure Marketplace.

After deployment completes, follow Next steps to reset the administrator password, configure access, DNS, and TLS, and verify the platform.

docs.title: Deployment options
docs.text:
The exact fields and available values depend on the selected Marketplace plan.

Use this page to understand the main deployment options. The Azure Marketplace form is authoritative for the options available to your deployment.

Option What it controls What to choose Can be changed later? Subscription Azure subscription where the managed application is deployed and billed Select the target subscription No — redeployment is required to move to another subscription Resource group Resource group containing the Azure Managed Application resource Select or create the application resource group No — treat as a deployment setting Region Azure region where the platform is deployed Select a supported region No — redeployment is required to move regions Application name Customer-visible name of the Managed Application Use your organization's naming standard Treat as a deployment setting Workload Primary platform use case Search or Observability Depends on supported iVedha workflows Capacity Initial platform capacity Small, Medium, or Large Yes, through supported iVedha capacity-change workflows Topology Elasticsearch node-role and data-tier layout Select one of the topologies available for the workload and plan Depends on supported iVedha workflows Machine learning Optional ML or inference capacity Enable only when required and available Depends on the selected plan and supported iVedha workflows Public access Whether public HTTPS endpoints are enabled Enable or disable Depends on supported iVedha network workflows DNS domain Domain used for Elasticsearch and Kibana service hostnames Platform-provided DNS domain or company-owned DNS domain Changing later can require DNS and certificate changes Maintenance window Preferred time for supported maintenance Select the day, time, time zone, and other options shown by the form Yes, through the supported iVedha maintenance workflow Elastic license Elastic license or entitlement used by the deployment Follow the license option provided by the selected plan Yes, through the supported license-management workflow Support contacts Contacts used for deployment notifications, service communication, and support Enter monitored organization contacts Yes, through supported iVedha configuration workflows when available

docs.title: Workload
docs.text:
Choose the primary platform use case:

  • Search
  • Observability

The workload determines which capacity and topology options are available.

See choose capacity and topology.

docs.title: Capacity and topology
docs.text:
Choose an initial capacity:

  • Small
  • Medium
  • Large

Then select one of the topology options available for the selected workload and Marketplace plan.

The initial capacity can be reviewed after deployment based on actual platform usage.

docs.title: Public access
docs.text:
Choose whether the platform exposes supported public HTTPS endpoints.

  • Enabled — public access is available after deployment.
  • Disabled — configure private connectivity after deployment.

Private Endpoint, routing, DNS, and certificate configuration are completed under Next Steps.

docs.title: DNS domain
docs.text:
Choose one of the supported DNS domain options:

  • Platform-provided DNS domain
  • Company-owned DNS domain

If you select a company-owned DNS domain, enter the domain or subdomain required by the Marketplace form.

The platform publishes the authoritative DNS targets after deployment.

docs.title: Maintenance window
docs.text:
Select the maintenance options exposed by the Marketplace form.

Depending on the plan, these can include:

  • occurrence or frequency;
  • day;
  • start time;
  • time zone;
  • duration.

The maintenance window can later be managed through the supported iVedha maintenance workflow.

docs.title: Support contacts
docs.text:
Enter the operational and support contact information requested by the Marketplace form.

The support email address is used for deployment lifecycle notifications, including:

  • deployment request received;
  • Marketplace deployment completed and onboarding in progress;
  • Your deployment is ready.

Use a monitored organization email address.

Never enter passwords, tokens, private keys, or other secrets in contact or free-text fields.

docs.title: Additional options
docs.text:
Some Marketplace plans can expose additional settings.

If an option is not described here:

  1. review the description in the Marketplace form;
  2. confirm what the option controls before changing the default;
  3. contact support if the effect of the setting is unclear.

For the deployment procedure, see Deploy from Azure Marketplace.

docs.title: Review deployment details
docs.text:
When platform provisioning is complete, a Your deployment is ready notification is sent to the support email address provided during Marketplace deployment.

This notification confirms that platform readiness checks have passed and provides the information required to continue with post-deployment configuration.

docs.title: Confirm deployment readiness
docs.text:
The ready notification includes:

  • deployment name;
  • deployment reference;
  • available application endpoints;
  • required next steps.

Keep the deployment reference. It can be used when contacting support about the deployment.

docs.title: Application endpoints
docs.text:
The notification provides the endpoints available for the deployment.

Depending on the selected configuration, these can include:

docs.title: Public endpoints
docs.text:
• Kibana
  • Elasticsearch
  • Fleet

Public endpoints are provided when public access is enabled.

docs.title: Private endpoints
docs.text:
• Kibana
  • Elasticsearch
  • Fleet

Private endpoints are used with the customer-side private connectivity configuration.

Use only endpoints provided by the platform. Do not construct endpoint names from Azure resource names or naming conventions.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
After receiving the deployment-ready notification, complete the remaining customer configuration:

  1. Reset the Elastic password
  2. Configure networking
  3. Configure DNS
  4. Configure certificates

These steps are covered in Next Steps.

The platform is deployed and ready at this point, but access can still depend on completing the required customer-side network, DNS, and certificate configuration.

docs.title: Need help?
docs.text:
Use the deployment reference from the notification when contacting support.

Continue to Next Steps.

docs.title: Monitor deployment
docs.text:
After selecting Create in Azure Marketplace, monitor the deployment until the managed platform is ready.

A successful Azure Resource Manager deployment does not necessarily mean Elasticsearch and Kibana are ready for use.

docs.title: Deployment stages
docs.text:
The deployment progresses through several stages.

Stage What it means Marketplace request accepted Azure has accepted the request to create the managed application Azure deployment Azure creates the Managed Application and required infrastructure Platform configuration Opsflw configures and reconciles the managed Elasticsearch platform Elasticsearch and Kibana ready The core platform services are running Endpoints published Elasticsearch, Kibana, DNS, and Private Link information is available Ready for Next Steps Post-deployment network, DNS, TLS, and access configuration can begin

Do not start post-deployment configuration until the platform has published the required deployment details.

docs.title: Deployment notifications
docs.text:
Deployment notifications are sent to the support email address provided during Marketplace deployment.

Notifications can include important deployment status updates and confirmation when the platform is ready for the next configuration steps.

Make sure the support email address entered during deployment is monitored and can receive messages from the platform.

The Azure portal remains the authoritative place to review the current Managed Application and deployment status.

docs.title: Open the managed application
docs.text:
1. In the Azure portal, search for Managed applications.
  2. Select your managed application.
  3. Confirm that the Azure provisioning state is successful.
  4. Open Resources and select My Deployment when available.
  5. Review the customer-visible deployment status.

Depending on the application version, the deployment view can show information such as:

  • workload profile;
  • capacity;
  • topology;
  • location;
  • health;
  • synchronization status.

docs.title: Understand Azure success versus platform readiness
docs.text: There are two important status layers.

docs.title: Azure deployment
docs.text:
Azure creates the Managed Application and its infrastructure.

If this stage fails, review the Azure deployment operations for errors such as:

  • permissions;
  • policy restrictions;
  • quota;
  • unsupported resource configuration.

docs.title: Managed platform readiness
docs.text:
After the Azure resources are created, Opsflw continues configuring the platform.

The deployment is ready to continue when:

  • Elasticsearch is ready;
  • Kibana is ready;
  • platform health is successful;
  • required service endpoints are published.

Do not modify resources in the managed resource group if platform configuration is still in progress.

docs.title: If deployment does not complete
docs.text:
Continue monitoring while deployment status is actively changing.

Use deployment issues if:

  • Azure reports Failed;
  • the deployment stops progressing;
  • Elasticsearch or Kibana does not become ready;
  • required endpoints are not published.

docs.title: Deployment complete
docs.text:
When Elasticsearch and Kibana are ready and the deployment details are available, continue to review deployment details.

The deployment details provide the values required for the post-deployment Next Steps.

docs.title: Contact support
docs.text:
Use iVedha support when a problem requires managed-platform investigation, configuration assistance, or engineering intervention.

Available support channels:

  • AI chat: https://chat.ivedha.cloud
  • Support portal: https://support.ivedha.com/

Use AI chat for guided troubleshooting and supported platform actions.

Use the support portal when you need a tracked support case or engineering investigation.

docs.title: Have the deployment reference ready
docs.text:
The most important identifier is the deployment reference from your deployment notification email.

Also provide, when relevant:

  • deployment name;
  • Azure region;
  • approximate start time of the issue;
  • affected service or workload;
  • whether the issue affects all users or only some users;
  • whether access is public or private;
  • relevant HTTP status codes;
  • Azure correlation ID when available;
  • redacted error messages;
  • troubleshooting steps already completed.

docs.title: Describe the impact
docs.text:
Explain the customer impact in practical terms.

Examples:

  • Kibana is unavailable to all users;
  • application indexing has stopped;
  • OpenTelemetry traces are no longer arriving;
  • one Elastic Agent policy is failing;
  • search latency has increased significantly;
  • deployment onboarding has not completed.

If your support agreement defines severity levels such as P1–P4, use the severity that matches the actual business impact.

docs.title: Useful diagnostic information
docs.text:
Depending on the issue, useful evidence can include:

  • DNS resolution results;
  • TCP connectivity results;
  • TLS verification output;
  • Elasticsearch HTTP status and redacted error;
  • Elastic Agent health status;
  • affected Fleet policy or integration name;
  • affected OpenTelemetry signal;
  • deployment or Azure correlation ID.

Keep diagnostic information focused on the failing component.

docs.title: Do not send secrets
docs.text:
Never include:

  • passwords;
  • one-time passwords;
  • API keys;
  • enrollment tokens;
  • access tokens;
  • authentication headers;
  • browser cookies;
  • private keys;
  • unredacted secret values.

If a workflow requires sensitive information, use the protected input or upload mechanism provided by iVedha.

docs.title: Customer data
docs.text:
Avoid sending production documents, log records, traces, or other customer data unless they are specifically required to investigate the issue.

When sample data is needed, use redacted or synthetic examples where possible.

docs.title: Support case updates
docs.text:
For an existing support case:

  • use the same case reference for follow-up;
  • update the case when business impact changes;
  • include new diagnostic evidence when it materially changes the investigation;
  • confirm when service has recovered.

Avoid opening multiple cases for the same active issue unless iVedha support asks you to do so.

docs.title: Azure-specific problems
docs.text:
Some issues are primarily Azure subscription or Marketplace problems rather than managed-platform issues.

Examples include:

  • Marketplace purchasing restrictions;
  • Azure Policy;
  • subscription quota;
  • Azure billing;
  • subscription-level permissions.

iVedha can help identify the likely ownership of the issue, but some Azure account or subscription problems may need to be resolved through your organization's Microsoft Azure support channel.

docs.title: Before contacting support
docs.text: If you have not already done so, start with Troubleshooting overview and collect the results of the relevant checks.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Application resource group Customer-controlled Azure resource group containing the Azure Managed Application resource. Azure Managed Application Azure Marketplace deployment model that creates an application resource together with a managed resource group containing the platform infrastructure. Capacity profile Initial platform sizing selection such as Small, Medium, or Large. Certificate signing request (CSR) Request generated by the managed platform and submitted to a certificate authority to obtain a TLS certificate. The platform retains the corresponding private key. Data stream Elasticsearch storage model commonly used for time-series data such as logs, metrics, and traces. Deployment reference Customer-facing identifier associated with a deployment and included in iVedha deployment notifications. Use it when requesting support or managed platform changes. Elastic Agent Elastic component used to collect telemetry, run integrations, and connect managed observability sources to Elasticsearch. Elastic connectors Elastic services that integrate supported external content sources or services with Elasticsearch workflows. Elasticsearch Distributed search, analytics, and data platform used for indexing, search, observability data, and vector or semantic-search workloads. Fleet Kibana-based management interface used to centrally manage Elastic Agents, agent policies, integrations, enrollment, and health. Fleet Server Service that coordinates communication between Fleet and enrolled Elastic Agents. Ingestion Process of sending data into Elasticsearch. Kibana Elastic browser interface for search, dashboards, observability, Fleet, security administration, and other supported Elastic features. Logstash Elastic data-processing service used for specialized ingestion, transformation, enrichment, and routing pipelines. Managed resource group Azure resource group containing the infrastructure operated as part of the Managed Application. Customers should not modify managed resources directly unless explicitly documented. OpenTelemetry (OTel) Open observability standard and ecosystem for producing and transmitting logs, metrics, and traces using common APIs, protocols, and semantic conventions. OpenTelemetry Collector Runtime component that receives, processes, enriches, and routes OpenTelemetry logs, metrics, and traces. OTLP OpenTelemetry Protocol used to transport telemetry between applications, collectors, agents, and observability backends. Private DNS DNS configuration that resolves service hostnames to private addresses for approved private networks. Private Endpoint Customer-owned Azure network interface that provides private connectivity to a supported service through a private IP address in a VNet. Private Link Azure private-connectivity technology used to access services without exposing the connection over the public internet. Private Link Service Service-side Azure resource to which a customer-created Private Endpoint connects. Use the deployment-provided resource information rather than reconstructing its resource ID. Public access Deployment configuration in which supported platform endpoints can be reached through public network paths, subject to TLS, authentication, and customer security controls. Search workload Platform use case focused primarily on indexing and querying application, document, knowledge, vector, or other search data. Observability workload Platform use case focused primarily on logs, metrics, traces, and operational analytics. Semantic conventions OpenTelemetry conventions that standardize the names and meaning of telemetry attributes and signals. Snapshot Elasticsearch backup stored in a configured snapshot repository and used for supported recovery workflows. Subject Alternative Name (SAN) Certificate field that identifies the hostnames for which a TLS certificate is valid.

The platform-generated CSR includes the required SANs for enabled deployment services such as Elasticsearch, Kibana, Fleet, and Logstash.

TLS Transport Layer Security protocol used to encrypt connections and verify service identity using certificates. Topology Elasticsearch deployment layout describing how node roles and data tiers are organized. Your deployment is ready iVedha notification indicating that managed-platform readiness checks have completed successfully. This is the customer-facing readiness signal for starting post-deployment configuration.

docs.title: Monitor health and capacity
docs.text:
iVedha continuously monitors the health of the managed platform. Customers remain responsible for monitoring the behavior and outcomes of their own workloads.

A healthy platform does not automatically mean that every application, ingestion source, query, dashboard, or telemetry pipeline is working as expected.

docs.title: What iVedha monitors
docs.text:
iVedha monitors managed-platform conditions such as:

  • Elasticsearch cluster health;
  • node and service availability;
  • storage and capacity conditions;
  • platform resource utilization;
  • managed Kubernetes and infrastructure health;
  • managed platform component availability.

When a platform condition requires intervention, iVedha can investigate and perform supported remediation.

Customers should not resize Kubernetes nodes, Elasticsearch nodes, disks, or other managed infrastructure directly.

docs.title: What customers should monitor
docs.text:
Customers should monitor workload outcomes such as:

  • application indexing success;
  • search and query behavior;
  • ingestion completeness;
  • Elastic Agent health;
  • Fleet policy and integration health;
  • OpenTelemetry logs, metrics, and traces arriving as expected;
  • dashboards and alerts showing current data;
  • application availability and service objectives.

For observability workloads, a healthy Elastic Agent or OpenTelemetry Collector does not by itself prove that every expected signal is arriving correctly. Validate the actual logs, metrics, and traces used by the workload.

docs.title: Review Elasticsearch health
docs.text:
Users with appropriate permissions can review high-level Elasticsearch cluster health.

curl --fail-with-body --user "<user>" \
  "https://<elasticsearch-hostname>/_cluster/health?pretty"

The main cluster states are:

Status Meaning Green Primary and replica shards are available Yellow Primary shards are available, but one or more replicas are unavailable Red One or more primary shards are unavailable

Persistent yellow or any red condition should be investigated.

Do not change shard allocation settings or other managed Elasticsearch infrastructure directly.

docs.title: Watch workload growth
docs.text:
Capacity requirements can change as workloads grow.

Review trends such as:

  • daily ingestion volume;
  • stored data;
  • retention period;
  • search and query demand;
  • observability signal volume;
  • number of monitored hosts, services, or applications;
  • expected business growth.

Short spikes do not necessarily require a permanent capacity change. Persistent growth or recurring pressure should trigger a capacity review.

docs.title: When to consider more capacity
docs.text:
Request a capacity review when you observe conditions such as:

  • sustained ingestion growth;
  • stored data approaching the expected profile range;
  • longer retention requirements;
  • sustained indexing or search pressure;
  • recurring capacity-related warnings;
  • significant new applications or telemetry sources;
  • expected business growth that materially changes the workload.

Capacity changes should be based on workload evidence rather than selecting a larger profile without understanding the requirement.

docs.title: Request a capacity review
docs.text:
Use the supported iVedha workflow:

  • AI chat: https://chat.ivedha.cloud
  • Support portal: https://support.ivedha.com/

Provide, when available:

  • deployment reference;
  • current ingestion rate;
  • current stored data;
  • retention requirement;
  • expected growth;
  • workload type;
  • relevant performance or capacity symptoms.

iVedha can review the workload and recommend a supported capacity change.

Do not resize managed Kubernetes, Elasticsearch, storage, or infrastructure resources directly.

For initial planning ranges, see Choose capacity and topology.

docs.title: Manage the Elastic license
docs.text:
The Elastic features available in your deployment depend on the active Elasticsearch license.

License configuration is managed through the supported iVedha workflow. Do not modify license-related managed resources directly.

docs.title: Check the active license
docs.text:
You can review the current Elasticsearch license using an authorized account.

curl --fail-with-body --user "<user>" \
  "https://<elasticsearch-hostname>/_license"

Review:

  • license type;
  • license status;
  • expiration date when applicable.

You can also review license information through Kibana when your role has the required permissions.

docs.title: License types
docs.text:
Depending on the Marketplace offer, deployment configuration, and your Elastic entitlement, the deployment can use:

  • Elastic Basic capabilities;
  • a trial license;
  • a customer-provided commercial Elastic license.

Do not assume that a Marketplace plan name automatically determines the Elasticsearch license level.

docs.title: Use your commercial Elastic license
docs.text:
If your organization has a commercial Elastic entitlement, request the license change through iVedha.

Use:

  • AI chat: https://chat.ivedha.cloud
  • Support portal: https://support.ivedha.com/

Identify the deployment and request an Elastic license update.

The workflow will guide you through the supported method for providing the required license information.

Do not send license material through normal chat messages, email, documentation, or support-ticket text when a protected upload or credential workflow is provided.

docs.title: Need help with Elastic licensing?
docs.text:
iVedha can also assist with Elastic license procurement, renewal, and licensing options.

This can include:

  • helping determine which Elastic subscription level fits the required features;
  • coordinating commercial license procurement;
  • assisting with renewal planning;
  • helping apply the license to the managed platform after purchase.

For licensing assistance, use:

  • AI chat: https://chat.ivedha.cloud
  • Support portal: https://support.ivedha.com/

When requesting assistance, include the deployment reference and the capabilities you need, but do not include existing license files or other sensitive commercial information unless requested through a protected workflow.

docs.title: Verify a license change
docs.text:
After the platform reports that the change has completed:

  1. allow a few minutes for synchronization;
  2. check the Elasticsearch license status again;
  3. confirm the expected license type is active;
  4. test the specific licensed capability you need.

If the license status does not change as expected, contact iVedha support and provide the deployment reference and the non-sensitive license status returned by Elasticsearch.

docs.title: License expiration
docs.text:
For licenses with an expiration date, plan renewal before the current entitlement expires.

An expired or changed license can affect features that require a commercial subscription.

Monitor the license expiration date and coordinate renewal with your Elastic licensing contact and iVedha as required.

docs.title: Protect license information
docs.text:
Do not:

  • store commercial license material in source control;
  • paste license files into documentation or tickets;
  • modify Kubernetes secrets or managed platform resources directly;
  • install unsupported tooling to change the platform license.

Use only the supported iVedha workflow for platform-level license changes.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Continue with back up and restore to understand data protection and recovery.

docs.title: Lifecycle states
docs.text:
The Azure Marketplace deployment and the managed platform onboarding process have separate lifecycle stages.

An Azure deployment can complete successfully before the managed Elasticsearch platform is ready for use.

docs.title: Deployment lifecycle
docs.text: Stage Customer meaning Customer action Deployment requested Azure Marketplace accepted the deployment request No action required Azure provisioning Azure is creating the Managed Application and its resources Monitor the Azure deployment Marketplace deployment completed Azure provisioning succeeded Wait while iVedha onboarding continues Onboarding in progress iVedha is configuring the platform and running readiness checks No action required unless an error is reported Deployment ready Platform readiness checks passed and customer endpoints are available Continue with post-deployment configuration Deployment failed Azure provisioning or managed onboarding could not complete Review the error and contact support when required Deleting Azure is removing the Managed Application and managed resources Wait for deletion to complete Deleted The Managed Application has been removed Complete cleanup of customer-owned resources

docs.title: Deployment requested
docs.text:
After Azure Marketplace accepts the request, iVedha sends a notification similar to:

Your request for <deployment> has been received

This confirms that the deployment request entered the managed onboarding process.

No customer action is normally required.

docs.title: Azure provisioning
docs.text:
Azure creates the Managed Application and the resources required by the selected Marketplace plan.

During this stage, Azure can report states such as:

  • Accepted;
  • Running;
  • Succeeded;
  • Failed.

These are Azure resource deployment states.

They do not by themselves indicate that Elasticsearch, Kibana, Fleet, or other managed services are ready.

docs.title: Marketplace deployment completed
docs.text:
When Azure provisioning succeeds, you can receive the notification Marketplace deployment completed — onboarding is in progress.

At this point:

  • the Azure Managed Application has been created;
  • required Azure infrastructure has been provisioned;
  • iVedha onboarding and platform configuration are still running.

Do not begin endpoint, DNS, certificate, or application configuration yet.

docs.title: Onboarding in progress
docs.text:
During onboarding, the managed platform performs configuration and readiness work required for the selected deployment.

This can include preparation of:

  • Elasticsearch;
  • Kibana;
  • Fleet and Fleet Server;
  • Elastic Agent;
  • OpenTelemetry components;
  • Logstash when enabled;
  • networking and ingress;
  • platform monitoring.

The exact internal steps can vary by platform version.

Customers do not need to monitor or modify these internal components.

docs.title: Deployment ready
docs.text:
The authoritative readiness event is the Your deployment is ready notification.

This means managed platform readiness checks have completed successfully.

The notification provides the deployment information required to continue, including available service endpoints.

Depending on the enabled components, these can include:

  • Kibana;
  • Elasticsearch;
  • Fleet;
  • Logstash.

After receiving this notification, continue with Next Steps:

  1. Reset the administrator password.
  2. Configure network access.
  3. Configure DNS.
  4. Configure TLS certificates.
  5. Verify access.

docs.title: Deployment failed
docs.text:
A deployment can fail during either:

  • Azure provisioning — for example because of policy, permissions, quota, Marketplace eligibility, or another Azure error.
  • Managed onboarding — Azure provisioning succeeds, but platform onboarding cannot complete.

Do not recreate the deployment immediately without understanding the failure.

See Deployment issues for troubleshooting guidance.

docs.title: Deleting
docs.text:
When the Azure Managed Application is deleted, Azure removes the managed application and its managed resource group.

Do not manually delete individual managed resources while deletion is running.

docs.title: Deleted
docs.text:
After Azure reports the Managed Application as deleted, the managed deployment is no longer available.

Customer-owned resources outside the managed resource group may still need cleanup, including:

  • Private Endpoints;
  • DNS records;
  • credentials;
  • application integrations;
  • telemetry destinations.

See Delete the application for the complete decommissioning process.

docs.title: Important distinction
docs.text:
Azure Succeeded does not mean platform ready.

Use the Your deployment is ready notification as the customer-facing readiness signal.

If Azure provisioning succeeds but the ready notification does not arrive, see Deployment issues or Contact support.

docs.title: Manage maintenance
docs.text:
The maintenance window defines the preferred time for planned platform changes that can affect service availability or performance.

The initial maintenance schedule is selected during Marketplace deployment.

Platform maintenance configuration is managed through the iVedha AI chat:

https://chat.ivedha.cloud

docs.title: Understand the maintenance window
docs.text:
The maintenance schedule includes:

  • day or recurrence;
  • start time;
  • time zone;
  • maintenance duration.

Always confirm the configured time zone when reviewing or changing the schedule.

Do not assume that the displayed time is UTC or your local workstation time.

docs.title: Before planned maintenance
docs.text:
Before a maintenance event that can affect service availability:

  • notify affected users and application owners;
  • confirm important applications can retry temporary connection failures;
  • review active incidents or business-critical processing;
  • avoid scheduling major customer-side changes during the same window when possible.

For observability workloads, temporary interruptions can cause agents or applications to buffer and retry telemetry.

For search workloads, applications should handle temporary Elasticsearch connection failures using appropriate retry behavior.

docs.title: Change the maintenance window
docs.text:
To request a maintenance-window change:

  1. Sign in to the iVedha AI chat application.
  2. Select or identify the deployment.
  3. Ask the assistant to change the maintenance window.
  4. Provide the requested day, start time, time zone, and other schedule information.
  5. Review the requested change.
  6. Confirm the change when prompted.
  7. Wait for confirmation that the new configuration has been applied.

Allow a few minutes for the updated configuration to synchronize.

docs.title: Verify the schedule
docs.text:
After the change completes, confirm the maintenance schedule through the supported iVedha workflow.

Make sure the configured:

  • day;
  • start time;
  • time zone;
  • recurrence

match the intended maintenance window.

docs.title: After maintenance
docs.text:
After a maintenance event, confirm that normal workload behavior has resumed.

Check:

  • Elasticsearch is available;
  • Kibana loads normally;
  • users can authenticate;
  • Elastic Agents return to Healthy in Fleet;
  • OpenTelemetry logs, metrics, and traces continue to arrive;
  • application indexing and searches are working.

iVedha monitors managed-platform health during and after supported maintenance operations.

docs.title: Emergency maintenance
docs.text:
Some urgent platform changes may need to occur outside the preferred maintenance window to protect availability, security, or data integrity.

When possible, iVedha will communicate the expected impact and status through the configured support contacts.

docs.title: Need help
docs.text:
If the maintenance schedule cannot be changed or service does not recover as expected:

  • AI chat: https://chat.ivedha.cloud
  • Support portal: https://support.ivedha.com/

Provide the deployment reference from your deployment notification.

Do not include passwords, API keys, private keys, or other secrets.

docs.title: Manage Elastic Agents with Fleet
docs.text:
The managed platform uses an OpenTelemetry-first observability architecture.

For new observability workloads:

  • OpenTelemetry is the standard telemetry model for logs, metrics, and traces;
  • Elastic Agent is the standard collection and telemetry gateway layer;
  • Fleet centrally manages Elastic Agents, policies, and integrations;
  • Elasticsearch stores and analyzes the resulting telemetry;
  • Kibana provides visualization, investigation, and observability workflows.
Applications / Hosts / Kubernetes / Azure Services
                         ↓
                    Elastic Agent
                         ↓
             OpenTelemetry integrations
                         ↓
        OpenTelemetry logs, metrics, traces
                         ↓
                    Elasticsearch
                         ↓
                       Kibana

The goal is to normalize observability data around OpenTelemetry semantic conventions and OTel-native data streams regardless of where the telemetry originates.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry is the common telemetry model
docs.text:
Logs, metrics, and traces should use OpenTelemetry conventions wherever supported.

This provides a common representation for telemetry coming from applications, virtual machines, Kubernetes, Azure services, databases, middleware, network and security systems, and custom sources.

Elastic integrations that still produce ECS-compatible events remain supported, but new observability designs should prefer OpenTelemetry-native telemetry where available.

docs.title: Elastic Agent is the collection layer
docs.text:
Elastic Agent provides the common collection layer for the managed observability platform.

Depending on the workload, Elastic Agent can:

  • receive OTLP telemetry from applications and collectors;
  • collect host logs and metrics;
  • collect Kubernetes telemetry;
  • collect Azure service telemetry;
  • run Elastic integrations;
  • collect custom logs and metrics;
  • enrich telemetry with infrastructure and resource metadata.

The objective is for the resulting observability data to align with OpenTelemetry conventions before it is analyzed in Elasticsearch.

docs.title: Fleet provides centralized management
docs.text:
Use Fleet in Kibana to manage Elastic Agents centrally.

Fleet manages:

  • agent enrollment;
  • agent policies;
  • OpenTelemetry integrations;
  • Elastic integrations;
  • configuration distribution;
  • agent health;
  • agent versions and upgrades;
  • enrollment and removal.

Avoid manually maintaining local configuration on Fleet-managed agents.
